items.subject: phy
items.q: Two masses of 5 g and 10 g are suspended from the two ends of a string passing over a massless, frictionless pulley. Calculate the acceleration of the system when the masses are left free:
items.explanation: Net pulling force = (10 − 5)g and total mass = 15 (same units), so a = 5g/15 = g/3.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A body of mass 3 kg moving with speed 10 m s⁻¹ hits a wall at an angle of 60° with the wall and returns at the same angle. The impact time was 0.2 s. Calculate the force exerted on the wall:
items.explanation: Only the velocity component normal to the wall reverses: v⊥ = 10 cos 30° = 5√3 m/s. Δp = 2 × 3 × 5√3 = 30√3 kg m/s, so F = 30√3/0.2 = 150√3 N.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A mass of 1 kg is thrown up with a velocity of 100 m/s. After 5 seconds, it explodes into two parts. One part of mass 400 g comes down with a velocity of 25 m/s. Calculate the velocity of the other part:
items.explanation: At 5 s, v = 100 − 10 × 5 = 50 m/s upward. Momentum is conserved in the explosion: 1 × 50 = 0.4 × (−25) + 0.6v ⇒ v = 100 m/s upward.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Calculate the net resistance of the circuit between A and B. (From A, one branch has 3 Ω then 4 Ω to B; the other branch has 6 Ω then 8 Ω to B; a 7 Ω resistor connects the junction between 3 Ω and 4 Ω to the junction between 6 Ω and 8 Ω.)
items.explanation: 3/4 = 6/8, so the Wheatstone bridge is balanced and the 7 Ω carries no current. R = (3 + 4) ∥ (6 + 8) = 7 × 14/21 = 14/3 Ω.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A capacitor is charged with a battery and the energy stored is U. After disconnecting the battery, another capacitor of the same capacity is connected in parallel with it. Then the energy stored in each capacitor is:
items.explanation: The charge q is shared equally, so each capacitor has q/2. Energy in each = (q/2)²/2C = (1/4)(q²/2C) = U/4.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Two projectiles of the same mass and with the same velocity are thrown at angles 60° and 30° with the horizontal. Which quantity will remain the same?
items.explanation: R = u² sin 2θ/g, and sin 120° = sin 60°, so complementary angles give the same range. Time of flight and maximum height depend on sin θ and differ.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A mass m tied to a string is performing vertical circular motion about centre O. A is the highest point, B the lowest point, and C and D are the ends of the horizontal diameter. If the average velocity of the particle is increased, at which point will the string break?
items.explanation: Tension is greatest at the lowest point, where T = mg + mv²/r and the speed is also maximum, so the string breaks first at B.

items.subject: phy
items.q:
For the given reaction, the particle X is:
¹¹₆C → ¹¹₅B + β⁺ + X
items.explanation: In β⁺ decay a proton changes into a neutron, emitting a positron and a neutrino (antineutrino goes with β⁻ decay).

items.subject: phy
items.q: A man is slipping on a frictionless inclined plane and a bag falls down from the same height. Then the speeds of both are related as:
options: v_B and v_m can't be related
items.explanation: With no friction, only gravity does work in both cases: ½mv² = mgh ⇒ v = √(2gh), independent of path, so both reach the bottom with equal speed.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A body of weight 72 N moves from the surface of the earth to a height equal to half the radius of the earth. The gravitational force exerted on it will be:

items.subject: phy
items.q: Rainbow is formed due to:
items.explanation: Sunlight is dispersed (refracted into colours) on entering raindrops and is internally reflected inside them before emerging, producing the rainbow.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Gravitational force is required for:
items.explanation: Natural convection works because warmer, less dense fluid rises and cooler, denser fluid sinks — buoyancy needs gravity. Conduction and radiation do not.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A plano-convex lens (µ = 1.5) has a radius of curvature of 10 cm. It is silvered on its plane surface. Find the focal length after silvering:
items.explanation: Lens focal length f_L = R/(µ − 1) = 20 cm; the plane mirror has infinite f. Power = 2/f_L = 1/10, so the system acts as a mirror of focal length 10 cm.

items.subject: phy
items.q: By the photoelectric effect, Einstein proved:
items.explanation: Einstein explained the photoelectric effect by treating light as photons, each of energy E = hν.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Maximum frequency of emission is obtained for the transition:
items.explanation: Upward transitions (1→2, 2→6) absorb. For emission, ΔE(2→1) ∝ 1 − 1/4 = 3/4 is larger than ΔE(6→2) ∝ 1/4 − 1/36 = 2/9, so 2→1 gives the highest frequency.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A hollow cylinder and a solid cylinder roll without slipping down an inclined plane. Which of these reaches the ground earlier?
items.explanation: a = g sin θ/(1 + k²/R²). The solid cylinder has k²/R² = 1/2 against 1 for the hollow one, so its acceleration is larger and it reaches first.

items.subject: phy
items.q: To find the degrees of freedom, the correct expression is:

items.subject: phy
items.q: The order of frequency for γ-rays (b), X-rays (a) and UV rays (c) is:
items.explanation: In the EM spectrum, frequency increases from UV to X-rays to γ-rays, so γ > X > UV, i.e. b > a > c.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The electric field at the centre O of a semicircle of radius a having linear charge density λ is given by:
items.explanation: By symmetry, components along the diameter cancel. Integrating the perpendicular components: E = ∫(kλ dθ/a) cos θ from −π/2 to π/2 = 2kλ/a = λ/(2πε₀a).

items.subject: phy
items.q: The width of a river is 1 km. The velocity of a boat is 5 km/h. The boat covers the width of the river by the shortest possible path in 15 min. Then the velocity of the river stream is:
items.explanation: Shortest path is straight across, at speed 1 km/0.25 h = 4 km/h. This equals √(5² − v²), so v = 3 km/h.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The motion of a particle is given by S = (3t³ + 7t² + 14t + 8) m. The acceleration of the particle at t = 1 s is:
items.explanation: v = dS/dt = 9t² + 14t + 14 and a = dv/dt = 18t + 14. At t = 1 s, a = 32 m/s².

items.subject: phy
items.q: A charge Q is situated at a corner of a cube. The electric flux passing through all the six faces of the cube is:
items.explanation: Eight such cubes would surround the charge completely, so one cube receives 1/8 of the total flux Q/ε₀, i.e. Q/(8ε₀).

items.subject: phy
items.q: Two long straight parallel wires, 5 m apart in the plane of the paper, carry currents of 5 A (left wire) and 2.5 A (right wire), both directed upward. The magnetic field at point P, midway between them (2.5 m from each), will be:
items.explanation: B = µ₀I/(2πr): the 5 A wire gives µ₀/π into the page (⊗) and the 2.5 A wire gives µ₀/2π out of the page at P. Net = µ₀/2π, into the page (⊗).

items.subject: phy
items.q: A charged particle having q/m equal to 10⁸ C/kg and velocity 3 × 10⁵ m/s enters a uniform magnetic field B = 0.3 T at an angle of 30° with the direction of the field. The radius of curvature will be:
items.explanation: Only v⊥ = v sin 30° = 1.5 × 10⁵ m/s causes circular motion. r = mv⊥/(qB) = 1.5 × 10⁵/(10⁸ × 0.3) = 5 × 10⁻³ m = 0.5 cm.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The value of the quality factor is:
items.explanation: For a series LCR circuit at resonance, Q = ω₀L/R = 1/(ω₀CR). Option (2) is dimensionally wrong.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Two stationary sources each emit waves of wavelength λ. An observer moves from one source to the other with velocity u. The number of beats heard by him per second is:
items.explanation: Moving towards one source raises the observed frequency by u/λ, and moving away from the other lowers it by u/λ. Beat frequency = 2u/λ.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A string is cut into three parts having fundamental frequencies n₁, n₂ and n₃ respectively. Then the original fundamental frequency n is related by the expression:
items.explanation: With the same tension and linear density, n ∝ 1/l. Since l = l₁ + l₂ + l₃, we get 1/n = 1/n₁ + 1/n₂ + 1/n₃.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The equations of two waves are given as x = a cos(ωt + δ) and y = a cos(ωt + α), where δ = α + π/2. The resultant motion represents:
items.explanation: With φ = ωt + α: x = −a sin φ, y = a cos φ, so x² + y² = a² (circle). At φ = 0 the point is at (0, a) and then x becomes negative, so it moves anticlockwise.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The relation between λ and T₁/₂ is (T₁/₂ = half-life, λ = decay constant):
items.explanation: Setting N = N₀/2 in N = N₀e^(−λt) gives λT₁/₂ = ln 2, so T₁/₂ = ln 2/λ = 0.693/λ.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The ratio W/Q for a Carnot engine is 1/6. Now the temperature of the sink is reduced by 62 °C, and this ratio becomes twice. Therefore the initial temperatures of the sink and source are respectively:
items.explanation: 1 − T₂/T₁ = 1/6 and 1 − (T₂ − 62)/T₁ = 1/3. Subtracting: 62/T₁ = 1/6 ⇒ T₁ = 372 K = 99 °C, and T₂ = 310 K = 37 °C.

items.subject: phy
items.q: In each circuit below a p-n diode (anode on the left, arrow pointing right) is in series with a resistor; the potentials of the left end and the right end are given. Which diode is in forward-biased condition?
options: Left end 0 V, right end −2 V
Left end 0 V, right end 2 V
Left end −5 V, right end −2 V
Left end 5 V, right end 12 V
items.explanation: A diode is forward biased when its p-side (anode) is at a higher potential than its n-side. Only in (1) is the anode (0 V) higher than the cathode side (−2 V).

items.subject: phy
items.q:
The given truth table is correct for:
A B | Y
1 1 | 1
1 0 | 0
0 1 | 0
0 0 | 0
items.explanation: Output is 1 only when both inputs are 1 — the AND gate.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The bob of a simple pendulum of length l is displaced from the mean position to an angular position θ with respect to the vertical. If it is released, the velocity of the bob at the lowest position is:
items.explanation: The bob falls through h = l(1 − cos θ). Energy conservation gives ½mv² = mgh ⇒ v = √(2gl(1 − cos θ)).

items.subject: phy
items.q: If F = (60 î + 15 ĵ − 3 k̂) N and v = (2 î − 4 ĵ + 5 k̂) m/s, then the instantaneous power is:

items.subject: phy
items.q: A uniform triangular lamina ABC is right-angled at B, with AB = 4, BC = 3 and AC = 5 (units). I₁, I₂ and I₃ are its moments of inertia about the sides AB, BC and AC respectively. The correct relation is:
items.explanation: For a triangular lamina about one side, I = Mh²/6, where h is the distance of the opposite vertex from that side. h = 3 for AB, 4 for BC, 2.4 for AC, so I₂ > I₁ > I₃.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Two spherical bobs of masses M_A and M_B are hung vertically from two strings of lengths l_A and l_B respectively. They are executing SHM with frequencies related as f_A = 2f_B. Then:
items.explanation: f = (1/2π)√(g/l) does not depend on the mass, and f ∝ 1/√l. Doubling f needs a quarter of the length: l_A = l_B/4.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Nuclear fission is best explained by:
options: Independent particle model of the nucleus
items.explanation: Bohr and Wheeler explained fission by treating the nucleus as a charged liquid drop that deforms and splits when excited.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Who evaluated the mass of the electron indirectly with the help of its charge?
items.explanation: Thomson had measured e/m. Millikan's oil-drop experiment measured e, and combining it with e/m gave the electron's mass indirectly.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A car battery of emf 12 V and internal resistance 5 × 10⁻² Ω receives a current of 60 A from an external source (i.e. it is being charged). Then the terminal voltage of the battery is:
items.explanation: While charging, current enters the positive terminal, so V = E + Ir = 12 + 60 × 0.05 = 15 V.

items.subject: phy
items.q: There are two bulbs of (40 W, 200 V) and (100 W, 200 V). The correct relation for their resistances is:
items.explanation: R = V²/P. At the same rated voltage, the lower-power bulb has larger resistance: R₄₀ = 1000 Ω and R₁₀₀ = 400 Ω.

items.subject: chem
items.q: According to Faraday's law of electrolysis, the mass deposited at an electrode is proportional to:
options: m does not depend on Q
items.explanation: Faraday's first law: m = ZQ = ZIt. The mass deposited is directly proportional to the charge passed.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A man 6 feet tall wants to see his full image. The required minimum length of the plane mirror will be:
items.explanation: A plane mirror only half your height, placed properly, shows your full image (from the laws of reflection), so 3 feet is needed.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The potentiometer is best for measuring voltage because:
options: It has a wire of high resistance
It measures p.d. as in a closed circuit
It measures p.d. as in an open circuit
items.explanation: At the balance point no current is drawn from the cell being measured, so the potentiometer reads its emf, i.e. the p.d. as in an open circuit.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A planet has a mass equal to the mass of the earth but a radius one-fourth the radius of the earth. The escape velocity for this planet will be:
items.explanation: v_e = √(2GM/R). With the same M and R/4, v_e doubles: 2 × 11.2 = 22.4 km/s.

items.subject: phy
items.q: The correct relation between α and β for a transistor is:
items.explanation: β = I_C/I_B and α = I_C/I_E with I_E = I_B + I_C. So β = I_C/(I_E − I_C) = α/(1 − α).

items.subject: chem
items.q: The life span of atomic hydrogen is:
items.explanation: Atomic hydrogen is very reactive; its atoms recombine into H₂ almost at once, so it lasts only a fraction of a second (about 0.3 s).

items.subject: chem
items.q: Cations and anions are arranged in alternate form in:
items.explanation: In ionic crystals such as NaCl, each ion is surrounded by oppositely charged ions, so cations and anions alternate in the lattice.

items.subject: phy
items.q: When an electron makes a transition from n = 4 to n = 2, the emitted line in the spectrum will be the:
items.explanation: Transitions ending at n = 2 form the Balmer series: 3→2 is the first line and 4→2 is the second line (Hβ).

items.subject: phy
items.q: A bubble in a glass slab (µ = 1.5) appears at 5 cm when viewed from one side and at 2 cm when viewed from the other side. The thickness of the slab is:
items.explanation: Real depth = µ × apparent depth: 1.5 × 5 = 7.5 cm from one face and 1.5 × 2 = 3 cm from the other. Thickness = 10.5 cm.

items.subject: phy
items.q: Which pair does not have equal dimensions?
items.explanation: Force is [MLT⁻²] but impulse (force × time) is [MLT⁻¹]. The other pairs have identical dimensions.

items.subject: chem
items.q:
Increasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic substitution for the following compounds:
(I) Benzene, (II) Toluene (C₆H₅CH₃), (III) Anisole (C₆H₅OCH₃), (IV) Benzotrifluoride (C₆H₅CF₃)
items.explanation: –CF₃ is strongly electron-withdrawing (deactivating), –CH₃ activates by hyperconjugation and –OCH₃ strongly activates by +R effect. So C₆H₅CF₃ < C₆H₆ < C₆H₅CH₃ < C₆H₅OCH₃.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Ethyl benzoate can be prepared from benzoic acid by using:
items.explanation: Esterification of an acid with an alcohol needs an acid catalyst (dry HCl or conc. H₂SO₄): C₆H₅COOH + C₂H₅OH → C₆H₅COOC₂H₅ + H₂O.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Polarization in acrolein (CH₂=CH–CHO) is shown as:
items.explanation: Conjugation with C=O pulls π-electrons towards oxygen: CH₂=CH–CH=O ↔ ⁺CH₂–CH=CH–O⁻. So the terminal CH₂ carries δ+ and oxygen carries δ−.

items.subject: chem
items.q: A —(reduction)→ B —(CHCl₃/KOH)→ C —(reduction)→ N-methylaniline. Then A is:
items.explanation: Working backwards: reduction of phenyl isocyanide (C) gives C₆H₅NHCH₃; C comes from aniline (B) by the carbylamine reaction; aniline is obtained by reducing nitrobenzene (A).

items.subject: chem
items.q: The first product of the reaction between RCHO and NH₂NH₂ is:
items.explanation: Hydrazine adds to the carbonyl group and loses water to give the hydrazone RCH=N–NH₂.

items.subject: chem
items.q: In the Friedel–Crafts reaction, toluene can be prepared by:
items.explanation: Friedel–Crafts alkylation: C₆H₆ + CH₃Cl (anhydrous AlCl₃) → C₆H₅CH₃ + HCl. CH₃COCl would give acetophenone.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which reagent converts propene to 1-propanol?
items.explanation: Hydroboration–oxidation adds water in an anti-Markovnikov way, giving CH₃CH₂CH₂OH. Acid hydration and oxymercuration give 2-propanol.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Reduction by LiAlH₄ of the hydrolysed product of an ester gives:
items.explanation: Hydrolysis of RCOOR′ gives RCOOH + R′OH. LiAlH₄ reduces the acid to RCH₂OH, so two alcohols result.

items.subject: chem
items.q: α-D-glucose and β-D-glucose are:
items.explanation: They differ only in configuration at C-1, the hemiacetal (anomeric) carbon, so they are anomers.

items.subject: chem
items.q: CF₂=CF₂ is the monomer of:
items.explanation: Tetrafluoroethylene polymerises to polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), known as Teflon.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The correct order of stability is:
items.explanation: More substituted alkenes are more stable (more hyperconjugation), so the 2-butenes beat 1-butene. The trans isomer avoids steric crowding of methyls, so it is the most stable.

items.subject: chem
items.q: 2-Butene shows geometrical isomerism due to:
options: Restricted rotation about the double bond
Free rotation about the double bond
Free rotation about the single bond
items.explanation: The π bond prevents rotation about C=C, so the two CH₃ groups can be fixed on the same side (cis) or opposite sides (trans).

items.subject: chem
items.q: The dihedral angle in the staggered form of ethane is:
items.explanation: In the staggered conformation each C–H on one carbon lies midway between two C–H bonds on the other, so the dihedral angle between nearest H's is 60°. 0° is the eclipsed form.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which one is responsible for the production of energy in biological reactions?
items.explanation: Thyroxine raises the basal metabolic rate, increasing oxidation of food and energy (heat) production in cells.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The average molar kinetic energies of CO and N₂ at the same temperature are related as:
options: Can't say anything, as volumes are not given
items.explanation: Average kinetic energy per mole = (3/2)RT depends only on temperature, not on the gas or its volume, so they are equal.

items.subject: chem
items.q: For the given energy E = 3.03 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, the corresponding wavelength will be (h = 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s):

items.subject: chem
items.q:
The equilibrium constant Kp for the following reaction is:
MgCO₃(s) ⇌ MgO(s) + CO₂(g)
items.explanation: Pure solids have unit activity and do not appear in the expression, so Kp = p(CO₂).

items.subject: chem
items.q: The correct relation between the dissociation constants of a dibasic acid is:
items.explanation: Removing the second H⁺ from an already negatively charged ion is harder, so the second dissociation constant is always smaller.

items.subject: chem
items.q: For any reversible reaction, if the concentration of reactants is increased, the effect on the equilibrium constant is that it:
options: Depends on the amount of concentration
items.explanation: The equilibrium shifts forward, but the equilibrium constant depends only on temperature, so it stays the same.

items.subject: chem
items.q: In a cubic crystal, A atoms are placed at every corner and B atoms at the centre of every face. The formula of the compound is:
items.explanation: A: 8 × 1/8 = 1 per cell; B: 6 × 1/2 = 3 per cell. The formula is AB₃.

items.subject: chem
items.q: In qualitative analysis of the second group in the lab, H₂S gas is passed in acidic medium for precipitation. When Cu²⁺ and Cd²⁺ react with KCN, under which of the following conditions will a precipitate (of CuS) not be formed, owing to relative stability?
options: K₂[Cu(CN)₄] – more stable; K₂[Cd(CN)₄] – less stable
K₂[Cu(CN)₄] – less stable; K₂[Cd(CN)₄] – more stable
K₃[Cu(CN)₄] – more stable; K₂[Cd(CN)₄] – less stable
K₃[Cu(CN)₄] – less stable; K₃[Cd(CN)₄] – more stable
items.explanation: Cyanide reduces Cu²⁺ to Cu⁺, forming the very stable K₃[Cu(CN)₄], which gives too few Cu⁺ ions for CuS to precipitate. K₂[Cd(CN)₄] is less stable, so CdS still precipitates (used to separate Cu and Cd).

items.subject: chem
items.q: The conjugate acid of NH₂⁻ is:
items.explanation: A conjugate acid has one extra proton: NH₂⁻ + H⁺ → NH₃.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which statement about pH and H⁺ is wrong?
options: The pH of neutral water is not zero
On mixing 1 N solutions (equal volumes) of CH₃COOH and NaOH, the pH will be seven
The pH of dilute, hot H₂SO₄ is more than that of concentrated, cold H₂SO₄
On mixing solutions of CH₃COOH and HCl, the pH will be less than 7
items.explanation: Neutralising a weak acid with a strong base gives CH₃COONa, which hydrolyses to make the solution basic (pH > 7). So statement (2) is wrong.

items.subject: phy
items.q: A 300 g radioactive sample has a half-life of 3 hours. After 18 hours the remaining quantity will be:
items.explanation: 18 h is 6 half-lives, so the amount left = 300/2⁶ = 300/64 ≈ 4.69 g (option 4.68 g).

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following compounds is electron deficient?
items.explanation: In BCl₃, boron has only six electrons in its valence shell, so it is the classic electron-deficient Lewis acid. (Monomeric BeCl₂ is also short of an octet, but BCl₃ is the standard answer.)

items.subject: chem
items.q: A dπ–pπ bond is present in:
items.explanation: Phosphorus has vacant 3d orbitals, so its π bond to oxygen in PO₄³⁻ is dπ–pπ. C and N have no d orbitals, so their π bonds are pπ–pπ.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which statement is wrong?
options: F is more oxidising than Cl
items.explanation: The F–F bond is weak (≈158 kJ/mol) because of repulsion between lone pairs on the small atoms; Cl₂ (≈242 kJ/mol) is stronger. The other statements are true.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which compound forms a linear polymer due to H-bonding?
items.explanation: The textbook example of chain-like H-bonded polymers is HF, which is not offered; H₂O forms a 3-D network and HCl/HBr hardly H-bond. The key gives NH₃; the question is dubious as printed.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The shape of Fe(CO)₅ is:
items.explanation: Fe(0) uses dsp³ hybrid orbitals for five CO ligands, giving a trigonal bipyramidal molecule.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The correct order of dissociation energy of N₂ and N₂⁺ is:
items.explanation: Bond order of N₂ is 3; N₂⁺ loses a bonding electron and has bond order 2.5. Higher bond order means a stronger bond, so N₂ has the higher dissociation energy.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Isoelectronic species are:
items.explanation: CO, CN⁻, NO⁺ and C₂²⁻ each have 14 electrons.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which ion is colourless?
items.explanation: Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰, so no d–d transition is possible and it is colourless. Cr⁴⁺ (d²), Ti³⁺ (d¹) and V³⁺ (d²) are coloured.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Mg is present in:
items.explanation: Magnesium is the central metal ion of the porphyrin ring in chlorophyll. Haemoglobin has Fe and vitamin B₁₂ has Co.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following elements exhibits the maximum oxidation state?
items.explanation: Mn (3d⁵4s²) can use all seven electrons, reaching +7 (as in KMnO₄). Cr reaches +6, V +5 and Fe usually +6 at most.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which of the following statements is correct for the stability of the anions of ethyl alcohol and phenol?
options: Delocalisation of π-electrons in phenoxide ion
Delocalisation of electrons in ethoxide ion
Inductive effect of ethyl and phenyl groups
Localisation of π-electrons in phenoxide ion
items.explanation: The negative charge on phenoxide is spread into the ring by resonance, stabilising it; ethoxide has no such delocalisation. That is why phenol is more acidic.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which compound has a planar structure?
items.explanation: XeF₄ (sp³d², two lone pairs) is square planar. XeO₂F₂ is see-saw and XeO₄ is tetrahedral. (XeOF₂ is T-shaped, which is also planar, but XeF₄ is the intended answer.)

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which complex compound will give four (geometrical) isomers?
items.explanation: [Fe(PPh₃)₃(NH₃)ClBr]⁺ is an octahedral Ma₃bcd type: one fac and three mer arrangements give four geometrical isomers. [Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ has only cis and trans forms.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which species does not exhibit paramagnetism?
items.explanation: CO has 14 electrons, all paired (like N₂). N₂⁺, O₂⁻ and NO each have an odd number of electrons, so they are paramagnetic.

items.subject: chem
items.q: For the disproportionation of copper, 2Cu⁺ → Cu²⁺ + Cu, E° is (given E° for Cu²⁺/Cu is 0.34 V and E° for Cu²⁺/Cu⁺ is 0.15 V):

items.subject: chem
items.q: A cell reaction is spontaneous when:
items.explanation: ΔG = −nFE; a reaction is spontaneous when ΔG is negative, which corresponds to a positive cell emf.

items.subject: chem
items.q: At infinite dilution, the conductances of Ba²⁺ and Cl⁻ ions are 127 and 76 ohm⁻¹ cm² respectively. The equivalent conductance of BaCl₂ at infinite dilution is:
items.explanation: 127 is the molar ionic conductance of Ba²⁺, so one equivalent (½Ba²⁺) contributes 63.5. Λ°eq(BaCl₂) = 63.5 + 76 = 139.5. (The paper calls both values 'equivalent conductances'; read literally that would give 203, so the question is loosely worded.)

items.subject: chem
items.q:
Given:
2Zn + O₂ → 2ZnO; ΔG° = −616 J
2Zn + S₂ → 2ZnS; ΔG° = −293 J
S₂ + 2O₂ → 2SO₂; ΔG° = −408 J
ΔG° for the reaction 2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂ is:

items.subject: chem
items.q: At 27 °C the latent heat of fusion of a compound is 2930 J/mol. The entropy change is:
items.explanation: For a phase change at equilibrium, ΔS = ΔH/T = 2930/300 = 9.77 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.

items.subject: chem
items.q: For the reaction C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(l), which one is true?
items.explanation: Only gases count: Δn(g) = 2 − 3 = −1, so ΔH = ΔE + Δn(g)RT = ΔE − RT.

items.subject: chem
items.q: For the reaction BrO₃⁻ + 5Br⁻ + 6H⁺ → 3Br₂ + 3H₂O, which of the following relations correctly represents the consumption and formation of reactants and products?
items.explanation: Rate = −(1/5) d[Br⁻]/dt = (1/3) d[Br₂]/dt. So d[Br₂]/dt = −(3/5) d[Br⁻]/dt. The minus sign appears because Br⁻ is consumed while Br₂ is formed.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Of the colligative properties of solutions, which one is the best method for determining the molecular weight of proteins and polymers?
items.explanation: Osmotic pressure gives a measurable value even for very dilute solutions of macromolecules, and it is measured at room temperature, so the biomolecules are not damaged.

items.subject: chem
items.q: Which one of the following is the method commonly used for the destruction of a colloid?
items.explanation: Added electrolyte ions neutralise the charge on colloidal particles, so they come together and settle (coagulation).

items.subject: chem
items.q: The volume of CO₂ (at STP) obtained by the complete decomposition of 9.85 g of BaCO₃ is:
items.explanation: BaCO₃ → BaO + CO₂. Moles = 9.85/197 = 0.05, which gives 0.05 mol CO₂ = 0.05 × 22.4 = 1.12 L.

items.subject: chem
items.q: The oxidation numbers of A, B and C are +2, +5 and −2 respectively. A possible formula of the compound is:
items.explanation: In A₃(BC₄)₂: 3(+2) + 2[5 + 4(−2)] = 6 − 6 = 0, so the compound is neutral. The other formulas do not balance.

items.subject: chem
items.q: R and S enantiomers differ in:
items.explanation: Enantiomers have identical physical and chemical properties in an achiral environment. They differ only in the direction in which they rotate plane-polarised light.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The first step for the initiation of photosynthesis will be:
options: Excitation of chlorophyll molecule due to absorption of light
items.explanation: Photosynthesis begins when chlorophyll absorbs a photon and an electron is excited. Photolysis, ATP formation and sugar synthesis all follow from this.

items.subject: bio
items.q: When plants are grown in magnesium-deficient but urea-rich soil, the symptoms expressed are:
items.explanation: Mg is the central atom of chlorophyll. Without it chlorophyll cannot form, so leaves turn yellow (chlorosis) even if nitrogen is plentiful.

items.subject: bio
items.q: For the synthesis of one glucose molecule, the Calvin cycle operates:
items.explanation: Each turn fixes one CO₂. A glucose molecule has six carbons, so six turns are needed.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Plants take up zinc in the form of:
items.explanation: Mineral nutrients are absorbed from the soil solution as ions. Zinc is taken up as the divalent cation Zn²⁺.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The bacterium generally used for genetic engineering (of plants) is:
items.explanation: Agrobacterium tumefaciens naturally transfers T-DNA from its Ti plasmid into plant cells, so it is widely used as a vector to make transgenic plants.

items.subject: bio
items.q: For the assimilation of one CO₂ molecule, the energy required in the form of ATP and NADPH₂ is:
items.explanation: In the C₃ (Calvin) cycle, fixing one CO₂ uses 3 ATP and 2 NADPH. For a whole glucose this becomes 18 ATP and 12 NADPH.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which is the first CO₂-acceptor enzyme in C₄ plants?
items.explanation: In mesophyll cells of C₄ plants, PEP carboxylase fixes CO₂ onto phosphoenolpyruvate to form oxaloacetate (a 4-C acid).

items.subject: bio
items.q: According to Mendelism, which character shows dominance?
items.explanation: In Mendel's pea, green pod colour is dominant over yellow. Terminal flowers and wrinkled seeds are recessive traits.

items.subject: bio
items.q: In the cross TTRr × ttrr, what percentage of the progeny will be tall and red-flowered?
items.explanation: TT × tt gives all Tt (tall). Rr × rr gives ½ Rr (red) and ½ rr. So tall and red = 1 × ½ = 50%.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which one shows the correct pairing?
items.explanation: Syphilis is caused by the spirochaete Treponema pallidum. AIDS is caused by HIV, gonorrhoea by Neisseria gonorrhoeae and typhoid by Salmonella typhi.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which one shows the correct pairing?
items.explanation: Cotton (Gossypium) belongs to Malvaceae. Sunflower is in Asteraceae, catechu (Acacia) in Mimosaceae and wheat in Poaceae.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Enzymes are not found in:
items.explanation: Viruses have no metabolic machinery of their own; they are just nucleic acid in a protein coat and use the host cell's enzymes. (A few carry special enzymes such as reverse transcriptase, but they have no metabolic enzymes.)

items.subject: bio
items.q: Viruses are considered living because:
items.explanation: Viruses have no metabolism or respiration, but they reproduce (replicate their genome) inside living host cells. This is their main living character.

items.subject: bio
items.q: If the apical bud has been removed, then we observe:
items.explanation: Auxin from the apical bud suppresses lateral buds (apical dominance). Removing the apex lets the lateral buds grow into branches, as is done in hedge pruning.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which hormone is responsible for fruit ripening?
items.explanation: Ethylene is the gaseous ripening hormone; it triggers the respiratory climacteric in fruits.

items.subject: bio
items.q: An eight-nucleate embryo sac is:
items.explanation: Eight-nucleate embryo sacs develop in monosporic (Polygonum type), bisporic (Allium type) and some tetrasporic types, so it may be any of these.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which is the cause of damage measured by relative biological effectiveness (RBE)?
items.explanation: RBE compares how much biological damage different kinds of ionising radiation cause for the same absorbed dose, so it relates to radiation damage. (The original key gives option 2.)

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which is responsible for the highest biomass in aquatic ecosystems?
items.explanation: The key gives benthic and brown algae; large kelps and other seaweeds form a huge standing biomass. The question is debatable, because phytoplankton such as diatoms account for most aquatic productivity.

items.subject: bio
items.q: A geocarpic fruit is:
items.explanation: In groundnut, the fertilised ovary is pushed into the soil and the fruit ripens underground (geocarpy). Carrot, radish and turnip are modified roots.

items.subject: bio
items.q: During double fertilisation, endosperm is formed by:
options: Two polar nuclei & one male gamete
One polar nucleus & one male gamete
Two polar nuclei & two male gametes
items.explanation: One male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei (or the secondary nucleus) to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

items.subject: bio
items.q: By which action does a seed coat become permeable to water?
items.explanation: Scarification scratches or softens a hard seed coat (mechanically or with acid) so water and oxygen can enter and germination can start.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What is true for mammals?
items.explanation: The duck-billed platypus is a prototherian (egg-laying) mammal. Bats have hair, elephants are viviparous and all mammals have a diaphragm.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following characters is not found in all chordates?
items.explanation: Notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal gill slits and a coelom are common to all chordates. A muscular diaphragm is found only in mammals.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The hairs (silk) found in the inflorescence of Zea mays are modifications of:
items.explanation: Corn silk consists of the very long styles of the female flowers, which end in stigmas and catch wind-borne pollen.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Pneumatophores are found in:
options: Vegetation found in marshy and saline lakes
items.explanation: Mangroves growing in marshy, saline, waterlogged places have negatively geotropic breathing roots (pneumatophores) to get oxygen.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The concentration of urine depends upon:
options: Network of capillaries arising from glomerulus
items.explanation: The loop of Henle sets up the medullary osmotic gradient by counter-current multiplication. Longer loops create a steeper gradient and allow more concentrated urine.

items.subject: bio
items.q: In which respect is the pulmonary artery different from the pulmonary vein?
items.explanation: Like other arteries, the pulmonary artery has a thick, muscular, elastic wall to bear the pressure of blood pumped by the ventricle. Veins have thinner walls and wider lumens.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The reason why hair loss is more in old age is:
items.explanation: With age, blood supply to the hair follicles decreases, so they get less nourishment and hair falls more. The key gives this answer.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What is the function of a Copper-T?
options: To inhibit implantation of the blastocyst
items.explanation: The key gives inhibition of implantation (the classical IUD action). NCERT also stresses that released Cu ions reduce sperm motility and fertilising capacity, so the question is debatable.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What is the function of the progesterone present in oral contraceptive pills?
options: To check entry of sperms into the cervix and make them inactive
items.explanation: Progestogens (with oestrogen) in the pill suppress FSH and LH release, so no ovulation occurs. They also thicken cervical mucus, but inhibiting ovulation is the main action.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Conversion of ammonia to urea is done by the ……… cycle:
items.explanation: In the liver, ammonia and CO₂ are converted to urea through the ornithine (Krebs–Henseleit) cycle.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What is the name of the joint between the ribs and the sternum?
items.explanation: The ribs join the sternum through costal (hyaline) cartilages, which form slightly movable cartilaginous joints.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The bone related to the skull is:
items.explanation: The pterygoid is a bone of the skull (palate region). The coracoid belongs to the pectoral girdle, the arytenoid is a laryngeal cartilage and the atlas is the first vertebra.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Melatonin is secreted by:
items.explanation: The pineal gland secretes melatonin, which regulates diurnal (sleep–wake) rhythms and pigmentation.

items.subject: bio
items.q: MSH is secreted by the:
items.explanation: Melanocyte-stimulating hormone comes from the pars intermedia (middle lobe) of the pituitary.

items.subject: bio
items.q: For a person eating boiled potato, the food contains the component:
options: Cellulose, which is digested by cellulase
DNA, which can be digested by pancreatic DNase
items.explanation: Potato cells contain nuclei, and their DNA is broken down by pancreatic DNase (nuclease). Humans lack cellulase, potato starch is digested and potato has no lactose.

items.subject: bio
items.q: In mammals, milk is digested by the action of:
items.explanation: Rennin in the gastric juice (especially of infants) curdles milk protein (casein) so it can be digested by pepsin.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What happens if a bone of a frog is kept in dilute hydrochloric acid?
items.explanation: Dilute HCl dissolves the calcium salts of the bone matrix. Only the organic (collagen/ossein) part is left, which is soft and flexible.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which disease of man is similar to the cattle disease bovine spongiform encephalopathy?
items.explanation: BSE ('mad cow disease') and Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease are both prion diseases that make the brain spongy.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Erythroblastosis foetalis is caused when the:
options: Female is Rh⁻ and male is Rh⁺
Female is Rh⁺ and male is Rh⁻
Female is Rh⁺ and male is Rh⁺
Female is Rh⁻ and male is Rh⁻
items.explanation: An Rh⁻ mother carrying an Rh⁺ foetus (inherited from an Rh⁺ father) makes anti-Rh antibodies. In a later pregnancy these destroy the foetal RBCs.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Depolarisation of the axolemma during nerve conduction takes place because:
options: Equal amounts of Na⁺ and K⁺ move out across the axolemma
Na⁺ moves inside and K⁺ moves more outside
items.explanation: On stimulation, voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open and Na⁺ rushes in, reversing the polarity (depolarisation). The K⁺ outflow that follows causes repolarisation. Option (2) is the closest choice.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which statement is true for WBCs?
options: They are manufactured in the thymus
They can squeeze through blood capillaries
items.explanation: Leucocytes can squeeze out through capillary walls (diapedesis) to reach sites of infection. They are nucleated and are formed mainly in the bone marrow.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which pair is correct?
items.explanation: Evaporation of sweat cools the body, so it helps regulate temperature. Sebum lubricates skin and hair, and the humerus is a bone of the forelimb.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which gland secretes an odorous secretion in mammals?
items.explanation: Anal (scent) glands produce strong-smelling secretions used for marking territory and defence, e.g. in skunks.

items.subject: bio
items.q: A characteristic of simple epithelium is that:
options: The cells form a definite layer
They continue to divide and help in organ function
items.explanation: A simple epithelium is a single, definite layer of closely packed cells resting on a basement membrane.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which food should be eaten in deficiency of rhodopsin in the eyes?
items.explanation: Rhodopsin is made from retinal (vitamin A). Carrot and ripe papaya are rich in β-carotene, a precursor of vitamin A.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which factor is responsible for the inhibition of an enzymatic process during feedback?
items.explanation: In feedback inhibition, the end product of a pathway accumulates and inhibits an early (often allosteric) enzyme of that pathway.

items.subject: bio
items.q: During viral infection, the protein formed in host cells to resist it is:
items.explanation: Virus-infected cells secrete interferons, which protect neighbouring cells against further viral infection.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The movement of ions against the concentration gradient will be by:
items.explanation: Moving ions uphill (from low to high concentration) needs energy from ATP and carrier proteins, which is active transport.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which is not a vestigial organ in man?
items.explanation: Nails are functional structures that protect the tips of fingers and toes. Wisdom teeth, the coccyx and the segmental abdominal muscles are vestigial.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Homo sapiens evolved in the:
items.explanation: Modern humans arose in the Pleistocene epoch of the Quaternary period.

items.subject: bio
items.q: A character closely related to human evolution is:
items.explanation: Reduction in jaw size and teeth, along with a larger cranium, is a key trend in hominid evolution. Loss of the tail, binocular vision and flat nails are shared with other apes and primates.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Darwin's finches are related to which evidence of evolution?
items.explanation: The finches of the Galápagos Islands, which radiated from a mainland ancestor into many island forms, are classic biogeographical evidence.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which one is directly (most closely) related to man?
items.explanation: Among the options, the gorilla (an African great ape) is closest to man. The chimpanzee is closer still but is not listed.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Lemurs (e.g. indri) are found in:
items.explanation: Lemurs, including the indri, are endemic to Madagascar, a well-known biodiversity hotspot.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Coconut milk is used in tissue culture because it contains:
items.explanation: Coconut milk (liquid endosperm) is rich in the cytokinin zeatin, which promotes cell division in cultures.

items.subject: bio
items.q: A giant rat (mouse) has been produced in the laboratory. The reason is:
items.explanation: The giant mouse was a transgenic animal made by inserting the rat growth-hormone gene into a mouse embryo, i.e. by gene manipulation (genetic engineering).

items.subject: bio
items.q: A plasmid is used as a vector because:
options: It is circular DNA which has the capacity to join to eukaryotic DNA
It can move between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells
items.explanation: A plasmid is a small, self-replicating circular DNA into which foreign (e.g. eukaryotic) DNA can be inserted, and which then carries it into a host. This is the key's answer; its marker genes are an added advantage.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Irregularities are found in Drosophila during organ differentiation; for example, long legs are formed in place of wings (or antennae). Which genes are responsible for this?
items.explanation: Homeotic (Hox) genes control the identity of body segments. Their mutations convert one structure into another, e.g. legs in place of antennae (Antennapedia).

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which cell organelle is concerned with the glycosylation of proteins?
items.explanation: Glycosylation of proteins begins in the rough endoplasmic reticulum and is completed in the Golgi apparatus. Of the options, only the ER fits.

items.subject: bio
items.q: A similarity between DNA and RNA is that:
items.explanation: Both are polynucleotides. They differ in sugar (deoxyribose vs ribose) and in one pyrimidine (thymine vs uracil), and RNA is the genetic material only in some viruses.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which aquatic fern is used to increase the yield of paddy crops?
items.explanation: Azolla harbours the nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium Anabaena in its leaves, so it is used as a biofertiliser in rice fields.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The plant group with the largest ovules, the largest trees and the largest gametes is:
items.explanation: Cycas has the largest ovules and gametes (antherozoids), and Sequoia, a gymnosperm, is the tallest tree.

items.subject: bio
items.q: In ferns, meiosis takes place at the time of:
items.explanation: The fern plant is the diploid sporophyte. Spore mother cells in the sporangia divide by meiosis to form haploid spores.

items.subject: bio
items.q: A similarity between Ascaris lumbricoides and Anopheles stephensi is:
items.explanation: In both, males and females look different (sexual dimorphism). Ascaris is not metameric and the mosquito is not an endoparasite.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The length of one turn (helical loop) of B-DNA is:
items.explanation: One complete turn of B-DNA contains about 10 base pairs, each 0.34 nm apart, giving a pitch of 3.4 nm (34 Å).

items.subject: bio
items.q: The primary function of the enteronephric nephridia of Pheretima is:
items.explanation: Nephridia are the excretory organs of the earthworm. Enteronephric nephridia pour nitrogenous wastes into the gut, which also helps conserve water.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Apis indica is the largest wild honey bee
Wax is a waste material of the honey bee
Karl von Frisch discovered the communication methods in honey bees
The drone of the honey bee is diploid
items.explanation: Karl von Frisch decoded the honey bee 'dance language' (printed as 'C.V. Fritsch'). Apis dorsata is the largest bee, wax is a secretion of the wax glands and drones are haploid.

items.subject: bio
items.q: ATP is a:
items.explanation: ATP has adenine, ribose and three phosphate groups, so it is a (ribo)nucleotide. Adenosine alone would be a nucleoside.

items.subject: bio
items.q: An essential amino acid is:
items.explanation: Phenylalanine cannot be synthesised by the human body and must come from the diet. Glycine, aspartic acid and serine are non-essential.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The anticodon occurs in:
items.explanation: The anticodon loop of tRNA has three bases that pair with the complementary codon on mRNA during translation.

items.subject: bio
items.q: In three-dimensional view, the tRNA molecule is:
items.explanation: The clover-leaf (2-D) structure of tRNA folds into a compact inverted-L shape in 3-D.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Saline solution is given to cholera patients because:
options: Na⁺ prevents water loss from the body
NaCl functions as a regulatory material
items.explanation: Cholera causes heavy loss of water and salts through diarrhoea. Saline (ORS) restores Na⁺, which helps the body retain water and corrects dehydration.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The function of telomeres in the nucleus is:
options: To seal the ends of chromosomes
items.explanation: Telomeres are repetitive DNA caps at chromosome ends. They seal the ends and prevent them from fusing or being degraded.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Spindle fibres attach to which structure of the chromosome?
items.explanation: Kinetochores are protein discs on the centromere where spindle microtubules attach.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following has carbohydrate as its prosthetic group?
items.explanation: Glycoproteins are conjugated proteins with carbohydrate attached. Chromoproteins have a pigment, lipoproteins a lipid and nucleoproteins a nucleic acid.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Viable material of endangered species can be preserved by:
items.explanation: Gene banks store living germplasm (seeds, pollen, gametes, tissues) under cryopreservation, so it can be used later.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The proteoglycan polysaccharide component in cartilage is:
items.explanation: Cartilage matrix contains chondroitin sulphate as its main glycosaminoglycan. Ossein is bone protein and casein is milk protein.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Mongolian idiocy, due to trisomy of the 21st chromosome, is called:
items.explanation: Trisomy 21 is Down's syndrome (formerly called mongolism). Turner's is 45,XO and Klinefelter's is 47,XXY.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What happens in plants during vascularisation?
options: Differentiation of procambium, formation of primary phloem followed by formation of primary xylem
Differentiation of procambium followed by the formation of primary phloem and xylem simultaneously
Formation of procambium, primary phloem and xylem simultaneously
Differentiation of procambium followed by the formation of secondary xylem
items.explanation: Procambium first differentiates from the meristem, and then it gives rise to primary xylem and primary phloem. The key treats these as forming simultaneously; in many plants protophloem actually matures a little earlier.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following ribosomes are engaged in protein synthesis in an animal cell?
options: Ribosomes which occur on the nuclear membrane and E.R.
Ribosomes of only the nucleolus and cytosol
Ribosomes of only mitochondria and cytosol
items.explanation: Ribosomes bound to the rough ER and the outer nuclear membrane actively make proteins (secretory and membrane proteins). This is the key's answer; free cytosolic ribosomes also synthesise proteins, so the options are imperfect.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The first cloned animal (mammal from an adult cell) was:
items.explanation: Dolly the sheep (1996, Roslin Institute) was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell by nuclear transfer.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following is the initiation codon?
items.explanation: AUG codes for methionine and is the start codon. UAG is a stop codon.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The method of DNA replication in which the two strands of DNA separate and each synthesises a new strand is:
items.explanation: Each daughter DNA keeps one parental strand and gets one new strand (shown by Meselson and Stahl), so replication is semiconservative.

items.subject: bio
items.q: In Drosophila the XXY condition leads to femaleness, whereas in human beings the same condition leads to Klinefelter's syndrome in males. This proves that:
options: In human beings the Y chromosome is active in sex determination
The Y chromosome is active in sex determination in both human beings and Drosophila
In Drosophila the Y chromosome decides femaleness
The Y chromosome of man has genes for the syndrome
items.explanation: In humans the Y chromosome (SRY gene) decides maleness whatever the number of Xs. In Drosophila sex depends on the X : autosome ratio and Y has no role in deciding sex.

items.subject: bio
items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does DNA replication occur?
items.explanation: DNA is synthesised (replicated) during the S (synthesis) phase of interphase.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Black rust of wheat is caused by:
items.explanation: Black (stem) rust of wheat is caused by the basidiomycete Puccinia graminis tritici. Ustilago causes smut and Albugo causes white rust.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following animals has scattered cells with cell–tissue grade organisation?
items.explanation: Cnidarians like Hydra are at the tissue (cell–tissue) grade, with cells loosely forming tissues. Sponges are at the cellular grade, while flukes and Ascaris have organs.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The blastopore is the opening of the:
items.explanation: During gastrulation, invagination forms the archenteron (primitive gut). Its external opening is the blastopore.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Cleavage in mammals is:
items.explanation: Mammalian eggs are alecithal (almost yolkless), so the whole egg divides into nearly equal blastomeres (holoblastic, roughly equal cleavage).

items.subject: bio
items.q: Extranuclear DNA is found in:
items.explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous organelles with their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Which of the following is used to manufacture ethanol from starch?
items.explanation: Brewer's yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, ferments sugars (from hydrolysed starch) to ethanol and CO₂.

items.subject: bio
items.q: A student observed an alga with chlorophyll a, chlorophyll d and phycoerythrin. It should belong to:
items.explanation: Red algae (Rhodophyta) have chlorophyll a and d together with the red pigment phycoerythrin.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Lysosomes contain:
items.explanation: Lysosomes contain acid hydrolases (proteases, lipases, nucleases, etc.) that digest materials inside the cell.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The role of enzymes in reactions is to:
items.explanation: Enzymes are organic (protein) catalysts. They speed up reactions by lowering the activation energy barrier.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What happens in the light reaction (photochemical reaction)?
items.explanation: The light reaction splits water, releases O₂ and produces ATP and NADPH. Sugar is made later in the dark (Calvin) reactions.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Most mutations are:
items.explanation: Most mutations disrupt a working gene, so they are harmful. Most are also recessive, because one normal allele usually still gives enough product.

items.subject: bio
items.q: The stored food in fungi is:
items.explanation: Fungi store carbohydrate as glycogen (and oil), like animals. Chitin is a structural cell-wall material, not stored food.

items.subject: bio
items.q: Living beings maintain continuity of life by:
options: DNA replication and its transfer to the next generation
items.explanation: Accurate copying of DNA and its passage to offspring keep hereditary information continuous from one generation to the next.

items.subject: bio
items.q: What will be the effect of the destruction of wild life?
options: Wild genes for disease resistance will not be obtained
items.explanation: Wild relatives of crops are a reservoir of useful genes such as disease resistance for breeding. Destroying wildlife loses this genetic resource for ever.
